translations.literal: [One] Now depose Qing and make him Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Note [1]: "Henceforth Liu Qing is deposed and made Prince of Qinghe."

translations.zh: 皇子□保育皇后，承訓懷艱，導達善性，將成其器。
translations.literal: The imperial son [lacuna in text] was reared by the Honored Lady, received instruction and bore hardship, was guided to a good nature, and would become his vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son [lacuna in text], reared by the Honored Lady, has been taught through hardship, guided toward a good nature, and is becoming fit for the role.

translations.zh: 蓋庶子慈母，尚有終身之恩，[二]豈若嫡後事正義明哉！
translations.literal: For a son of a concubine, a foster mother may still have a lifelong bond; [two] how can that compare with an heir of the principal wife serving clear righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: A foster mother may cherish a concubine's son all her life, Note [2]: but how can that compare with the clear justice owed to the lawful heir!

translations.literal: Now establish [lacuna in text] as Imperial Heir Apparent.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao is hereby established as crown prince."

translations.zh: 遂出貴人姊妹置丙舍，使小黃門蔡倫考實之，皆承諷旨傅致其事，[三]乃載送暴室。
translations.literal: Thereupon the Honored Lady and her sister were sent out to the Bing quarters; the junior yellow gate attendant Cai Lun was ordered to verify the matter; all followed the indirect instruction and attached the affair; [three] then they were loaded and sent to Baoshi.
translations.idiomatic: The Song sisters were then removed to the Bing apartments. The junior eunuch Cai Lun was ordered to investigate; all followed the empress's veiled instructions and fabricated the case, Note [3]: and the sisters were sent to the Baoshi.

translations.literal: The two Honored Ladies at the same time drank medicine and killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Both Honored Ladies took poison and died together.

translations.zh: [四]帝猶傷之，□掖庭令葬於樊濯聚。
translations.literal: [Four] The emperor still grieved for them; [lacuna in text] the director of the Rear Palace buried them at Fanzhuo cluster.
translations.idiomatic: Note [4]: The emperor still mourned them and ordered the director of the imperial harem to bury them at Fanzhuo.

translations.literal: [Five] Thereupon Yang was dismissed and returned to his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Note [5]: Yang was then dismissed and sent back to his home commandery.

translations.zh: 郡縣因事復捕系之，楊友人前懷令山陽張峻、左馮翊沛國劉均等奔走解釋，得以免罪。
translations.literal: The commandery and county, taking advantage of the affair, again arrested and detained him; Yang's friends, the former Huai magistrate Zhang Jun of Shanyang and Liu Jun of Pei in Zuofengyi, ran about explaining and secured his release from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials seized the occasion to arrest him again, but his friends—the former Huai county magistrate Zhang Jun of Shanyang and Liu Jun of Pei in Zuofengyi—interceded on his behalf and secured his release.

translations.literal: Yang lost heart, grew haggard, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Broken in spirit, Yang wasted away and died at home.

translations.zh: 慶時雖幼，而知避嫌畏禍，言不敢及宋氏，帝更憐之，□皇后令衣服與太子齊等。
translations.literal: Qing, though young at the time, knew to avoid suspicion and fear calamity; in speech he dared not mention the Song clan; the emperor pitied him all the more; [lacuna in text] the empress ordered clothing equal to the heir apparent's.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a boy, Liu Qing knew to avoid suspicion and never spoke of the Song family. The emperor pitied him all the more, and the empress ordered that his clothing match the crown prince's.

translations.zh: 太子特親愛慶，入則共室，出則同輿。
translations.literal: The heir apparent was especially close to and fond of Qing; entering, they shared a chamber; going out, they rode the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was especially fond of Liu Qing: indoors they shared a room; abroad they rode together.

translations.zh: 及太子即位，是為和帝，待慶尤渥，諸王莫得為比，常共議私事。
translations.literal: When the heir apparent took the throne—this is Emperor He—he treated Qing with especial generosity; none of the princes could compare; they often discussed private affairs together.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince succeeded as Emperor He, he treated Liu Qing with exceptional favor, beyond any other prince, and they often conferred in private.
